12. Thus, the basic dispute revolves around the question of competence to act as the manager of the school managed by the Society.
There are two factions among the members of the Society and several litigations are pending between them claiming superior rights against each other.

However,
the crucial aspect to be noticed is that, the last 2025:KER:37018 undisputed election was conducted in the year, 2011 in which Sri.Joseph Kattathara was elected as the President of the Society and consequently, he was also appointed as the manager of the said school.
Such appointment was approved as per Ext.P2 order passed by the 5th respondent as well, on 14.1.2013.
Even though the faction represented by Sri. Joseph Kattathara contends that a further election was later conducted on 20.02.2018, it was denied by the faction led by Sri. A.P.Abdul Sathar.

According to Sri. A.P.Abdul Sathar, no election was conducted on 22.02.2018, but instead, subsequent election was conducted on 27.9.2020, in which, the said Sathar was elected as the President and also as the manager of the said school.
Therefore, the basic question to be considered is, whose appointment is to be granted approval.

It has to be noted in this regard that as per the bye-laws of the society,
the tenure of the governing committee was three years.

However, even while passing an order approving the tenure of appointment of Sri. Joseph Kattathara for three years from 04.07.2014, a specific reference was made to the meeting conducted on 20.02.2018.

This would mean that for fixing the tenure for a prior period, a meeting held on 20.2.2018 was relied on and this would indicate a complete non application of mind by the 5 th respondent while passing Ext.P6 order.

If the approval of appointment of Sri. 2025:KER:37018 Joseph Kattathara was to be granted based on the decision taken on 20.02.2018, under no circumstances that could have been for a tenure prior to 20.02.2018.

It is to be noted that going by the tenure fixed in Ext.P6, it stood expired even prior to the date of the meeting held on 20.02.2018.

Anyhow, the said order was modified vide Ext.P7 by the 3rd respondent, with a direction to conduct an election.
However, Ext.P7 order was subsequently withdrawn as per Ext.P9 and the 5th respondent was directed to reconsider the question of approval of Sri. Joseph Kattathara.

In the meantime, when the approval of Sri.Joseph Kattathara was to be reconsidered by the 5th respondent, the claim of the 6th respondent as the manager also came up based on an election claimed to have been conducted on 27.09.2020.
Both the claims were considered by the 5th respondent and Ext.P12 order was passed rejecting both the said applications.

opennyai_summary.facts:
The undisputed election to the President of the Society was conducted during the meeting of the general body on 3.7.2011.
In the said election, Sri. Joseph Kattathara was elected as the President and consequently, he was appointed as the Manager of the school by the Executive Committee.
Even though the period of Joseph Kattathara expired during the year,
2014, as per the terms of the bye-laws, he continued as the Manager, in view of the fact that, as per clause 46 of Ext.P1 bye-laws, the governing body could be continued even after expiry of the tenure, until a new elected body as per the bye- laws takes charge of the affairs of the Society.
Besides, in Ext.P2 order of approval, no time limit was also prescribed.
3. In the meantime, the 6th respondent in WP(C)No.8780/2023- Sri, A.P.Abdul Sathar filed O.S.No.11/2018 before the Munsiff Court, Payyannur, seeking a mandatory injunction against the defendants therein, which include the Society, Sri. Joseph Kattathara and Sri. Sunil Kumar, the Secretary of the Society, to conduct the election to the governing body of the Society.
All the defects were cured and the application was resubmitted as per Ext.P4 on 11.04.2019.
As there was delay in considering the application for approval of the Manager, the petitioner filed WP(C)No.8815/2019 before this Court, which was disposed of as per Ext.P5 judgment, directing the 5 th respondent, to take a decision on the application for approval, within a time frame.
Acting upon the same, the 3rd respondent passed Ext.P7 order on 26.12.2019 cancelling Ext.P6 order with a further direction to the 4 th respondent to conduct election to the management committee of the school.
As per Ext.P9, the 5 th respondent-AEO was directed to reconsider the question of approval of appointment of Sri.Joseph Kattathara as the Manager of the school.
As per Ext.P11, the Review Petition was disposed of directing the 3 rd respondent to consider the question of approval of the manager, after hearing Sri. Joseph Kattathara.
In WP(C)No.15904/2021, an interim order was passed directing to maintain the status quo as on the date of order, with regard to the continuance of Sri. Joseph Kattathara as the manager of the school.
Based on the representation made by the former Secretary, this Court disposed of the said case with a direction to conduct the election.
However, in the operative portion of Ext.P6, the tenure of appointment of Sri. Joseph Kattathara was fixed as three years from 04.07.2014, which obviously refers to the period immediately after the expiry of the original period of Sri. Joseph Kattathara based on the election conducted in the year, 2011.
opennyai_summary.issue: Therefore, the basic question to be considered is, whose appointment is to be granted approval.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
However, even while passing an order approving the tenure of appointment of Sri. Joseph Kattathara for three years from 04.07.2014, a specific reference was made to the meeting conducted on 20.02.2018.
This would mean that for fixing the tenure for a prior period, a meeting held on 20.2.2018 was relied on and this would indicate a complete non application of mind by the 5 th respondent while passing Ext.P6 order.
Despite the fact that, the said Joseph Kattathara claimed the right to act as the manager contending that in the election conducted on 20.02.2018, he was elected as the President of the Society as well as the manager of the school,
no steps have been taken by the 6th respondent to challenge the same.
As far as Ext.P15 order passed by the 5 th respondent, approving the appointment of the 6th respondent as the manager, is concerned, under no circumstances, the 5 th respondent should have passed such an order in view of the fact that, the application submitted by the 6 th respondent already stood rejected as per Ext.P12 order.
Even in the absence of the interim 2025:KER:37018 order passed by this court, the 5 th respondent could not have passed Ext P15, as it amounts to the review of the Ext P12 order, which power is not vested with him.
opennyai_summary.decision:
v) The 6th respondent never challenged the decision taken on 20.02.2018, before a competent civil court, despite the fact that, his suit was pending consideration at the relevant time.
As against Ext.P12, the petitioner as well as the 6th respondent filed writ petitions and in WP(C) No 15904/2021 there was an order of status quo in the matter of continuation of Sri. Joseph Kattathara as the manager was passed on 6.08.2021.
Therefore, the 5 th respondent could not have reviewed Ext.P12 order and passed an order in the nature of Ext.P15 on 17.12.2021.
Moreover, Ext P15 order was passed without any reference to the Ext P12 order.
Therefore, on that reason, Ext.P15 cannot be treated as a legally sustainable one.
Now it is discernible from the averments made by the petitioner in I.A.No.1/2024 in WPC No.30637/2021 that, a further meeting has been conducted for electing the governing body of the society on 04.05.2024 and according to the petitioner therein, a new executive committee has been elected.
In such circumstances, in the light of the observations made above, WP(C)Nos.8780/2023,
15904/2021 and 30637/2021 are disposed of quashing Exts.P12 and P15 orders with a direction to the 5th respondent to approve the appointment of Sri. Joseph Kattathara as the Manager for the respective periods.
As far as WP(C) No.10955/2021 is concerned, in the light of quashing of Ext.P12 produced in WP(C)No.8780/2023 (Ext.P14 in WP(C) 10955/2021), it is disposed of but rejecting the relief number (ii) therein.
Appropriate orders in this regard shall be passed by the 5 th respondent within a period of two months from the date of receipt of a copy of this judgment.
